primary_claim: Narrow sentiment fine-tuning of GPT-2 does not simply overwrite pretrained representations but reconfigures and 'squishes' the model's output and activation space, concentrating sentiment information in middle-to-late layers while sharply degrading general language modeling (perplexity) on non-sentiment inputs.
stated_future_work: analyze scaling effects in larger models
test whether other fine-tuning objectives induce similar transformations
limitations_stated: sentiment direction's stability across datasets and architectures needs further validation
unclear how much of the shifting embedding space alignment is intrinsic vs. an artifact of dimensionality reduction
findings aren't entirely novel and may seem trivial
signs of slight overfitting beginning at epoch 3
quote: fine-tuning does not simply overwrite pre-trained representations but reconfigures them entirely, redistributing sentiment-specific information across layers and squishing the output representation space
